s1-armstrong-numbers.trick: Count decimal digits, then sum each digit raised to that count; compare with the original number.

s1-check-for-prime.trick: A composite number has a factor no larger than its square root.

s1-check-palindrome.trick: Reverse the number the same way as above, then compare it to the original.

s1-count-digits.trick: Repeatedly divide by 10 until it's 0, counting each division. Zero itself has exactly one digit.

s1-counting-frequencies-of-array-element.trick: Increment a hash-map count for each value; the map is the frequency table.

s1-gcd-or-hcf.trick: Euclid's algorithm: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b). Keep replacing the pair until b hits 0 — a is the answer.

s1-print-all-divisors.trick: Every divisor below sqrt(n) pairs with n/divisor; collect both and sort for ascending output.

s1-reverse-a-number.trick: Pull the last digit off with n % 10, push it onto the answer with rev*10 + digit, then drop the last digit from n.

s1-understand-recursion-by-print-somethi.trick: Every call does one unit of work, reduces n by one, and stops at zero; the base case prevents infinite recursion.

s1-print-name-n-times-using-recursion.trick: Print once, then recurse for the remaining n-1 copies; stop when n is zero.

s1-print-1-to-n-using-recursion.trick: Recurse to n-1 before outputting n, so the values appear in ascending order.

s1-print-n-to-1-using-recursion.trick: Output n before recursing to n-1, giving descending order.

s1-sum-of-first-n-numbers.trick: Use the recurrence sum(n) = n + sum(n-1), with sum(0) = 0.

s1-reverse-an-array.trick: Swap the outer pair and move both pointers inward until they cross.

s1-check-if-a-string-is-palindrome-or-no.trick: Compare matching characters from both ends; one mismatch disproves a palindrome.

s1-fibonacci-number.trick: Keep only the previous two Fibonacci values; each next value is their sum.

s1-find-the-highest-lowest-frequency-ele.trick: Count with a hash map, then scan counts for maximum and minimum; choose the smaller value on ties.

s1-user-input-output.trick: Extract typed values with >> and print results with <<; input is checked before use.

s1-data-types.trick: Choose types by range and purpose: int for ordinary integers, long long for larger sums, double for fractions, and string for text.

s1-if-else-statements.trick: Test conditions from the most specific case to the fallback; only the first matching branch runs.

s1-switch-statement.trick: Switch selects one matching integral case. Return from each case so execution cannot fall through.

s1-what-are-arrays-strings.trick: An array-like vector stores indexed values; a string stores indexed characters. Both use zero-based indices.

s1-for-loops.trick: Use a for loop when the range or iteration count is known in advance.

s1-while-loops.trick: Use a while loop while a condition remains true; update its state to ensure it terminates.

s1-functions-pass-by-reference-and-value.trick: A value parameter is copied; a reference parameter aliases the caller's variable and can change it.

s1-time-complexity-learn-basics-and-then.trick: Count how often the dominant operation runs; nested full loops multiply, while consecutive loops add.

s1-patterns.trick: For each row, print a predictable number of symbols; nested loops turn the pattern rule into code.

s1-c-stl.trick: C++ STL containers and algorithms provide tested building blocks; sort, binary search, and hash maps are common DSA tools.
s1-c-stl.time: O(n log n) for sorting; O(log n) search

s1-java-collections.trick: This lesson is about Java collections; the C++ equivalents are vector for ArrayList, unordered_set for HashSet, and unordered_map for HashMap.

s1-factorial-of-n-numbers.trick: Generate factorials 1!, 2!, ... only while the next multiplication stays at most the limit.
s1-factorial-of-n-numbers.time: O(k), k factorials not exceeding limit

s1-hashing-theory.trick: Hash tables map keys to buckets, giving expected constant-time insert and lookup. Use them to count frequencies.
